title: Product of Two Run-Length Encoded Arrays
summary: Given two run-length encoded arrays encoded1 and encoded2, expand each into full arrays nums1 and nums2 respectively.
statement: Given two run-length encoded arrays encoded1 and encoded2, expand each into full arrays nums1 and nums2 respectively. Compute the element-wise product of nums1 and nums2 to form a new array prodNums. Compress prodNums into a run-length encoded array with the minimum possible length and return it. Each encoded1[i] = [vali, freqi] describes the i^th segment of nums1, and each encoded2[j] = [valj, freqj] describes the j^th segment of nums2. Both nums1 and nums2 have the same length.
constraints: Each [value, frequency] pair has positive integers.
Each encoding has at most 100000 runs.
The two expanded arrays have equal length; return the shortest valid encoding of their products.
hints: Only the current run from each encoding can affect the next product segment.
Consume the smaller remaining frequency, advancing whichever run is exhausted.
Append a new product run unless its value equals the previous product, in which case merge frequencies.
Each step consumes a nonempty aligned interval; these intervals partition both arrays and adjacent equal products are merged immediately.
editorial: Each step consumes a nonempty aligned interval; these intervals partition both arrays and adjacent equal products are merged immediately.

tests.explanation: Both product regions equal six, so they merge into the single run [6,6].
Aligned run boundaries produce product runs [2,3], [6,1], and [9,2].
